Part 1 of 10 · Level-0 cross-functional process landscape · as specified · every gate (G) and hard block (HB) placed on the step it governs · 8 September 2026
Magnus Workspace Platform · Process Maps and RACI
Lanes = departments the platform defines · Columns = the order value moves
Suppliers quote, deliver, and are paid
Purchase order from the bill of materials →
Issue material and equipment to site
HB6 — signed contract to leave setup
Mobilise → deploy workforce → nine construction blocks →
Daily toolbox meeting — precondition of every site report
Incident → corrective action → closure · near miss ·
HB6 — signed contract for orders and funds
Milestones → progress claims → certification · write-offs by

Order and fund request refused without a
HB1–HB5 enforced at the step they guard · toolbox meeting

⚠ Where the live build deviates from this map today (each is detailed in Parts 2–9): RC-A one same-person check in sixteen approval controls · RC-B the write-off gate is chosen from a dropdown, not derived from the amount

Register: 25 of 30 gate labels and all 6 hard blocks on the live rows predate this specification, so no approver is ever named on screen · RC-H nothing notifies anyone · RC-N the live "Hard Block 6" blocks fund requests, not purchase orders
A step, or a chain of steps, performed by that lane. Arrows are implied left to right; each column hands to the next.
An approval gate: number · primary approver (Accountable) · alternate (Consulted) · working-day window where set. Thirty gates; 13–17 reserved.

A hard block: nobody can waive it — the step cannot happen until the precondition exists. Six, closed list. ● specification gap ⚠ live deviation Key: CEO Chief Executive Officer · COO Chief Operating Officer · PM Project Manager · Custodian Warehouse Custodian · 2d/3d working-day window
